key_insight: A Bayesian finite element model reconstructs steady blood-flow velocity and pressure from noisy, under-resolved measurements while explicitly quantifying uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This provides a training-free, physics-constrained way to estimate clinically important flow metrics such as pressure drop, flow rate, and wall shear stress in patient-specific vascular geometries.
method: Taylor-Hood finite element basis for velocity and pressure
Physics-informed maximum-entropy priors on nodal degrees of freedom
MAP inference via sparse nonlinear least squares with analytic pressure elimination; Laplace approximation for uncertainty
evidence_signal: On patient-specific cerebral aneurysm, aortic aneurysm, and coarctation cases, the method outperformed tricubic interpolation, matched PINN-level reconstruction quality, and improved wall-shear-stress recovery.
watch_item: The approach relies on a steady-flow assumption and accurate noise/priors; performance may degrade when measurements are very sparse, strongly unsteady, or boundary conditions are highly misspecified.
paper_title: Bayesian finite element regression for vascular flow reconstruction with quantified uncertainty
